citations.verbatim_statement: Assumption D.1 (Topologically ordered interventional targets). We assume there are exactly N environments {k₁, …, k_N} where each node j ∈ [N] undergoes one imperfect intervention in environment k_j. The interventional targets 1 ⪯ · · · ⪯ N preserve the topological order. We believe that identifying the topological order is another subproblem orthogonal to identifying the latent variables. Corollary D.1 (Identifiability from single node imperfect intervention per node). Given N environments satisfying Asm. D.1, the ground truth latent variables z can be identified up to element-wise diffeomorphism by combining both marginal and score invariances under our framework.

attestation.note: Main verified arXiv 2409.02772v2 at Assumption D.1, its immediately following remark, and Corollary D.1 on 2026-09-06; transcription combines the exact scope and conclusion sentences with notation normalized from PDF extraction.

env.world: A latent causal model on \(n\) scalar variables. Fix \(n\in\mathbb N\), the labeled vertex set \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), a finite labeled directed acyclic graph \(G\) on \([n]\) with parent sets \(\operatorname{pa}_G(i)\), and a sign vector \(s\in\{-1,+1\}^n\). The latent state is \(V=(V_1,\ldots,V_n)\in[0,1]^n\). A mechanism is a pair of families \(((p_i,q_i))_{i=1}^n\) in which \(p_i:[0,1]^{1+|\operatorname{pa}_G(i)|}\to(0,\infty)\) is the observational conditional density of \(V_i\) given \(V_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}\) and \(q_i:[0,1]\to(0,\infty)\) is the parent-independent perfect-intervention density at target \(i\), with distribution function \(Q_i(v)=\int_0^v q_i(u)\,du\). The observational latent law is \(p^0(v)=\prod_{i=1}^n p_i(v_i\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})\) and the target-\(i\) interventional latent law is \(p^i(v)=q_i(v_i)\prod_{\ell\ne i}p_\ell(v_\ell\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(\ell)})\). Write \(j\lessdot_G i\) when \(j\) is a strict ancestor of \(i\) in \(G\) with no vertex strictly between them in the ancestral order. The model stratum \(\Theta_{G,s}\) is the set of mechanisms that are positive, normalized, \(C^3\), causally minimal for \(G\), and of prescribed own-coordinate log-ratio derivative signs \(s\), carrying the relative product \(C^2\) topology. Three distinguished points of this world are the sparse witness \(\theta^{\mathrm{sp}}\), the cancellation witness \(\theta^{\mathrm{can}}\), and the nodewise normalized affine path \(\theta^t\), \(t\in[0,1]\), interpolating a mechanism toward \(\theta^{\mathrm{sp}}\).

The ancestral cover relation \(j\lessdot_G i\) is `CovBy` (Mathlib.Order.Defs.PartialOrder / Mathlib.Order.Cover) for the strict order induced by `DAG.isAncestor`; the note's `an ancestral cover in a DAG is a directed edge` step is then `CovBy` unfolded against `DAG.isAncestor_child`. Mechanisms are `ContDiffOn ℝ 3` positive normalized densities on closed cubes; the relative product \(C^2\) topology is the sup-norm-through-order-two topology on the finite product of mechanism slots, defined locally. env.world: The observed environment family generated by a shared mixing map. Let \(f:[0,1]^n\to\mathcal X\) be a \(C^2\) diffeomorphism onto the observed support \(\mathcal X\), the same map in every environment, and let \(X=f(V)\) be the observation. For \(e=0\) the observed law \(P^e\) is the pushforward of \(p^0\) under \(f\); for \(e\in[n]\) it is the pushforward of \(p^{\pi(e)}\), where \(\pi\) is an unknown bijection from interventional environment labels to latent intervention targets. The environment-label DAG \(G^\pi\) is the pullback of \(G\) by \(\pi\): \(j\to i\) in \(G^\pi\) exactly when \(\pi(j)\to\pi(i)\) in \(G\). The observable invariants are the density ratios \(R_i=dP^i/dP^0:\mathcal X\to(0,\infty)\), which after unmixing equal \(q_{\pi(i)}(v_{\pi(i)})/p_{\pi(i)}(v_{\pi(i)}\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(i))})\), together with their logarithms \(L_i=\log R_i\).

Built over `MeasureTheory.Measure.map` (Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Map, verified) for \(P^e\) and `ContDiffOn ℝ 2` plus an explicit two-sided inverse for the diffeomorphism; \(\pi\) is an `Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`; \(G^\pi\) is `Causalean.DAG` transported along that permutation. The proofs use \(R_i\) only through its unmixed latent form \(r_i(v)=q_i(v_i)/p_i(v_i\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})\), so the Jacobian cancellation is a single change-of-variables lemma in this S-block.

env.world: The Gaussian-kernel discrepancy layer on ratio laws. Let \(k(a,b)=\exp(-(a-b)^2)\) on \(\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\), with values in \((0,1]\) and \(k(a,a)=1\). For \(j\ne i\) the population discrepancy is \(D_{ji}=\operatorname{MMD}_k(\operatorname{Law}_{P^0}(R_i),\operatorname{Law}_{P^j}(R_i))\), the distance between the two kernel mean embeddings, and the second-moment contrast is \(F_{ji}=\mathbb E_{P^j}[R_i^2]-\mathbb E_{P^0}[R_i^2]\). Inside the model stratum, \(\mathcal V_{G,s,\pi}\) is the set of mechanisms with \(F_{\pi^{-1}(j)\pi^{-1}(i)}\ne0\) on every edge \(j\to i\) of \(G\), and \(\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}\) is the set with \(D_{ji}>0\) whenever \(\pi(j)\lessdot_G\pi(i)\). The observable directed graph \(H_D\) on interventional environment labels has arrow \(j\to i\) exactly when \(D_{ji}>0\).

env.world: The population decoder. Fix a topological ordering of \(H_D\) and let \(B_i\subseteq[n]\) be the environment labels preceding \(i\) in it. Let \(C_i(t\mid\ell_{B_i})=P^i(L_i\le t\mid L_{B_i}=\ell_{B_i})\), taken in its continuous version on the model support, and let \(U_i(x)=C_i(L_i(x)\mid L_{B_i}(x))\) be the identified rank coordinate. The population recovery map \(\mathscr D\) sends \((P^0,\ldots,P^n)\) to \((H_D,(U_i)_{i=1}^n,G^\pi)\): it forms every \(R_i\) and \(D_{ji}\), builds \(H_D\), selects a topological ordering, constructs every \(U_i\), aligns environment \(i\) with \(U_i\), and at each \(i\) returns as parent set the unique inclusion-minimal \(A\subseteq B_i\) with \(U_i\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}_{P^0}U_{B_i\setminus A}\mid U_A\).

env.world: Independent multi-sample sampling with sample splitting. Within each environment \(e\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\) the \(N_e\) observations are independent draws from \(P^e\), and the training and evaluation folds are independent; \(\underline N=\min_{0\le e\le n}N_e\). On the training folds a density-ratio estimate \(\widehat R_i:\mathcal X\to(0,\infty)\) is fitted without the evaluation observations; \(a_N\in[0,\infty)\) is a deterministic radius for the joint evaluation-law \(L^1\) error of those fitted ratios, holding with probability at least \(1-\eta\). On the independent evaluation folds \(\widehat D_{ji}\) is the norm of the difference of the empirical Gaussian-kernel mean embeddings of \(\widehat R_i(X)\) under environments \(0\) and \(j\). With familywise level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and first-stage failure level \(\eta\in(0,1)\), the simultaneous confidence radius is \(\varepsilon_N(\alpha,\eta)=2\sqrt2\,a_N+2[1+\sqrt{2\log(n(n+1)/\alpha)}]/\sqrt{\min_e N_e}\), and the sample-split confidence graph \(\widehat H\) has arrow \(j\to i\) exactly when \(\widehat D_{ji}-\varepsilon_N(\alpha,\eta)>0\).

env.world: The bounded statistical subclass and the generated-rank frontier. Fix a smoothness index \(\beta\in(2,\infty)\), a lower-envelope constant \(c\in(0,1)\), a uniform regularity constant \(M\in(1,\infty)\), an interior margin \(\rho\in(0,1/2)\), and a compact evaluation domain \(K\subseteq\operatorname{int}(\mathcal X)\). Write \(\mathcal Z_i(K)=\{L_{B_i}(x):x\in K\}\) and let \(g_i\) be the density of \(L_{B_i}(X)\) under \(P^i\), with \(g_i\equiv1\) when \(B_i=\varnothing\). The bounded Holder subclass \(\Theta^\beta_{G,s}(c,M,K,\rho)\subseteq\Theta_{G,s}\) collects the mechanisms obeying a bounded Holder radius, a density lower envelope, an own-derivative margin, a common interior domain, bounded shared mixing geometry, observed log-ratio regularity, and a conditional design envelope. With \(d_\star=\max_{i\in[n]}|B_i|\), a first-stage rate \(b_N\downarrow0\) and failure sequence \(\eta_N\downarrow0\), and a bandwidth \(h_N\downarrow0\), the simultaneous first-stage event is \(\mathcal E_N^\infty(b_N)=\{\max_{i\in[n]}\|\log\widehat R_i-\log R_i\|_{C^1(\mathcal X)}\le b_N\}\) and the target coordinate rate is \(r_N=h_N^2+\sqrt{\log(\underline N)/(\underline N h_N^{d_\star})}+b_N/h_N\). In this world \(\widehat U_i\) denotes a second-stage cross-fitted conditional-CDF estimator of \(U_i\) and \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{rank}}\) the local-linear conditional-CDF and generated-covariate linearization handle; neither is given a determinate construction here.
env.notes: All of \(\beta,c,M,\rho,K,\mathcal Z_i(K),g_i,d_\star,b_N,\eta_N,h_N,\mathcal E_N^\infty,\Theta^\beta,r_N\) are determinate and are defined formally. Per decision P-D2, \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{rank}}\) and \(\widehat U_i\) are NOT given Lean constructions: the core marks \(\widehat U_i\) an `open statistical construction` and \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{rank}}\) an `open-question handle`, and the frozen OEQ text says the handle does not yet provide a second-stage weight convention. They are bound here as named narrative symbols recorded inside the descriptive `String` payloads of `def:generated-rank-handle` and `oeq:generated-rank-frontier`. non_blocking_upstream_debt.description: Causalean/ML/Kernel/RKHS.lean contains only `Causalean.ML.IsRKHS`, a one-field structure carrying the reproducing identity `f x = ⟪f, representer x⟫` — no unit-norm feature-map interface, no kernel mean embedding, no MMD, no characteristic-kernel theorem, and no bounded-feature concentration. That is why round-4 decision P-D9 makes the whole kernel layer local here: this note builds `UnitNormFeatureMap`, `meanEmbedding`, the explicit \(\ell^2\) Gaussian feature map, and MMD in `Helpers/Kernel.lean`. A future promotion of that layer into `Causalean/ML/Kernel/` would be reused by any later kernel two-sample work. Not blocking: nothing here is deferred on it.

The generic measure-level graphoid layer in `Causalean/Mathlib/CondIndep/CondExp.lean` has weak union (`condIndepFun_weak_union_of_prodMk`, line 545), left extension, and contraction, but no INTERSECTION property — correctly, since intersection is not a semi-graphoid axiom and requires strict positivity. It also has no packaged coordinate-pair splitting lemma for Finset-indexed coordinate families. This note proves `condIndep_intersection_of_pos` (round-4, decision P-D10) and the bridge `condIndep_coordSplit_prodMk` (round-5, decision P-D11) locally, the first from its own positive-density assumption and the second from `MeasurableSpace.comap` algebra. Promoting both into `Causalean/Mathlib/CondIndep/CondExp.lean` would complete the generic graphoid layer for later work; note that the SCM/SWIG-typed `Causalean/SCM/Do/SemiGraphoid.lean` is NOT the right home, since it is not instantiable outside a `Causalean.SCM`. Not blocking: both lemmas are proved in scope here and add no assumption.

`lem:bounded-rkhs-empirical-mean` is a general fact (unit-norm Hilbert-valued i.i.d. empirical mean deviation via McDiarmid) with no causal content; it is a natural promotion target for `Causalean/Stat/Concentration/`. Not blocking: it is proved in scope here.
